Silence.SoundHint: When enabled, overrides the playlist's silence time between repeats.

Bounds.Title: Silence Boundaries
Bounds.ThresholdSettingHint:
“Find silence” uses this threshold unless the Sound has its own saved value.
Lower values detect quieter sounds. Higher values ignore faint noise.
Default: −60 dBFS.
Bounds.ThresholdHint: Lower values detect quieter sounds. Higher values ignore faint noise.
Bounds.ResetPending: The full file is selected. Save the Sound to reset its boundaries.
Bounds.Proposed: Suggested section: {start}–{end} s. Save the Sound to apply these boundaries.
Bounds.AllSilent: No audible section was found at this threshold. Boundaries were not changed.
Bounds.Unsupported: This file format is not supported by silence search.
Bounds.Failed: Could not analyze audio: {reason}. You can still enter boundaries manually.
Bounds.InvalidBounds: Enter valid boundaries: 0 ≤ start < end ≤ file duration.
Bounds.InvalidThreshold: Enter a number from −120 to 0 dBFS.
Bounds.InvalidPlayback: Saved boundaries for {name} are invalid or refer to another file. Playing the full file.
Bounds.Stale: The analyzed file path has changed. Check these boundaries again.
Bounds.PathChanged: The file path changed. Analyze again or check the boundaries manually.

HideRestrictedPlaylists.Name: Hide Sound Names from Players
HideRestrictedPlaylists.Hint: Shows players only the time and volume for sounds in Currently Playing, hiding all other details. Players with at least Observer access to a playlist can still see the details.

DisableRevisionChecks.Name: Disable revision checks
DisableRevisionChecks.Hint:
Enable only when global playlists are managed from one client.
Speeds up global playlist operations by skipping additional file checks. If several clients manage playlists at the same time, their changes may overwrite each other. A technical failure during a multi-file operation may save only part of the changes.

KeepPlayingOnConfigSave.Name: Preserve playback
KeepPlayingOnConfigSave.Hint: When enabled, “Update Sound” and “Update Playlist” do not stop playback if nothing changed or if only these properties changed: name, volume, repeat, fade duration, silence threshold (dBFS), description, playback mode, and playlist sorting.

MaxBufferDuration.Name: Buffering threshold (seconds)
MaxBufferDuration.Hint:
Sounds whose duration exceeds this threshold are streamed instead of buffered. Changes apply to future loads. Already loaded or cached sounds keep their playback type until the client reconnects.
Foundry's default is 600 seconds.

GlobalArchive.Hint: Inspect and restore deleted or replaced global playlists and folders.

ConflictMenu.Hint: Check local and global playlists or folders for matching IDs and keep both items if needed.

ConflictResolution.Name: ID conflict resolution
ConflictResolution.Hint:
Keep local: show the local item in this world and hide the global item with the same ID.
Keep both: give the local item a new ID, update its links, then show the global item.
Always ask: let the GM choose on entering the world.
Closing the dialog temporarily keeps the local item.

DuckStrength.Name: Audio ducking during preview
DuckStrength.Hint: 0% leaves other sounds unchanged. 100% silences music, environment, and interface sounds during preview.

SoundRowBudget.Name: Minimum displayed sounds
SoundRowBudget.Hint: The number of sound rows kept in the list across all expanded playlists. This increases automatically when a taller window needs more rows. A lower value reduces interface load but may update rows more often while scrolling. A higher value keeps more nearby rows ready but increases interface load.

Archive.MoveConflictIntro: Local item “{name}” has the same ID as a global item.
Archive.MoveConflictEffect:
To continue the move, the local item will receive a new ID and its links in this world will be updated.
It will then become a separate global item.
Archive.NoConflicts: No local and global playlist or folder IDs conflict in this world.
Archive.ConflictIntro:
A local item and a global item have the same ID.
The local item remains available here. The global item remains saved and available in other worlds.
Archive.ConflictKeep: To keep both, the local item receives a new ID and its links in this world are updated.
